comment: Columns whose VALUES must never be copied into the audit trail. tools/check-tenancy.mjs reds when any of them appears as a captured column in an audit.write_row(...) trigger argument, and reds again when an entry here names a column no migration creates — so the list cannot quietly go stale as the schema moves under it. This is not a general PII inventory and does not pretend to be one: it is the deny-list for ONE mechanism, and its job is to make the easy mistake (capturing a value because the value is what you wanted to see) impossible without a reviewed diff. The audit trail defaults to metadata — WHICH columns changed, not what they became — precisely so that this list rarely has to be consulted at all. SOURCE: docs/adr/20260202-audit-trail.md

columns.reason: A person's name. Copying it into the trail republishes it to every rank-30 admin of every org the subject belongs to, none of whom can read profiles directly.
The invitee's email address, which is the one identifier in this schema that reaches a human directly. It also belongs to someone who is not yet a member and has consented to nothing.
